title: Rabbi Shmuel bar Natan
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a student of Rabbi Hanina, as we find: "Rabbi Shmuel bar Natan said in the name of Rabbi Hanina" in Avodah Zarah 74a, Bekhorot 11a.
And in Sukkah 43b, in the dispute between Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shmuel bar Natan, reporting Rabbi Hanina.

And in Shabbat 38a: "Shmuel bar Natan said in the name of Rabbi Hanina: When Rabbi Yosi went to Tzippori he found hot water [on Shabbat], and he did not forbid it to them; [but] shriveled eggs he forbade to them," for Rabbi Hama son of Rabbi Hanina said: "Once I and my father were guests." Hyman finds the reading of the Jerusalem Talmud, Shabbat 3:1, preferable: Rabbi Assi said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosi: "Father went up to his house and found hot water there"; Rabbi Shmuel bar Natan in the name of Rabbi Hama son of Rabbi Hanina [and he related that the incident was as follows, that Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosi said]: "I and my father went up to Hammat Gader, and they brought before us eggs," etc. And indeed he spoke in the name of Rabbi Hama son of Rabbi Hanina in Berakhot ch. 1, halakhah 4, folio 10 [side unspecified]; Terumot 2:3; Gittin 4:6.

notes.text: The vocalized William Davidson text of Sukkah 43b names the first disputant Rabbi Elazar; it styles Shmuel Rav and puts בר נתן in brackets. The notice gives Rabbi Shmuel bar Natan.
The Berakhot locator gives chapter 1, halakhah 4, followed by -י, read here as folio 10 without specifying a side.

The inspected Bavli Shabbat 38a gives the hot-water/egg account and then “I and my teacher,” where Hyman supplies “I and my father.” The inspected Jerusalem Talmud 3:1 has Yosi reporting Yishmael and Shmuel reporting Chama bar Chanina, with “I and my father”; Hyman gives Assi and adds his own bracketed reassignment to Yishmael. These differences are preserved rather than harmonized.
